name: FLOOR.MATH
description: FLOOR.MATH rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance, accepting any sign combination and adding a mode argument to control how negative numbers are rounded.
tldr: Rounds down to a multiple of significance, with a mode for negative numbers.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value you want to round.

parameters.name: significance
parameters.description: The multiple to round to. Defaults to 1 if omitted.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Controls rounding of negative numbers. 0 (default) rounds toward zero; any other value rounds away from zero (more negative).

basicExample.description: Round down to the nearest integer
basicExample.explanation: With default significance 1 and mode 0, 24.3 rounds down to 24.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers: toward zero vs away from zero
advancedExamples.description: Mode 0 rounds toward zero; a non-zero mode rounds away from zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: Mode 0 rounds -5.5 toward zero, giving -5. With mode 1 it would give -6.

advancedExamples.title: Round to a chosen decimal multiple
advancedExamples.explanation: 6.0 is the multiple of 0.1 at or below 6.05.

howItWorks: FLOOR.MATH rounds number down to the nearest multiple of significance (default 1). Unlike classic FLOOR, it permits any sign combination. The mode argument only affects negative numbers: mode 0 rounds toward zero, and any other value rounds away from zero.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: Only available in Excel 2013 and later (and Microsoft 365); older versions return #NAME?.
For positive numbers, mode has no effect; it always rounds down.
Workbooks saved for pre-2013 compatibility will not support this function.

commonErrors.cause: Used in an Excel version earlier than 2013.
commonErrors.fix: Use FLOOR, or open the file in Excel 2013+ / Microsoft 365.
Use numeric values or numeric references.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports FLOOR.MATH with the same arguments and behavior in current versions.

faq.question: What does the mode argument do?
faq.answer: Mode only matters for negatives: 0 (default) rounds toward zero, any other value rounds away from zero.

faq.question: Is FLOOR.MATH available in older Excel?
faq.answer: No, it was introduced in Excel 2013. Use FLOOR in older versions.

faq.question: How is it different from FLOOR?
faq.answer: FLOOR.MATH lifts the sign restriction and adds mode control; classic FLOOR errors on mismatched signs.
